A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETVA work. All 22 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, references, and supplementary material, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original correlations with human judgments, question-generation and question-answering ablations, and evaluations of T2V models, including supplementary benchmark results in Table 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and additionally tabulates critical-reflection ablation scores in Table 3.

M1.justification: The scene-graph question-generation pipeline, knowledge augmentation, multi-stage answering procedure, and score aggregation are unchanged. The appendix prompts also remain identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use ETVABench-2k and ETVABench-105 with the same prompt sources, ten semantic categories, and evaluation scenarios. No dataset or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BLIP-ROUGE, BLIP-BLEU, CLIPScore, UMTScore, ViCLIPScore, and VideoScore; Table 2 retains vanilla question generation. The critical-reflection ablation newly tabulated in v2 was already discussed in v1.

E3.justification: Model configurations, benchmark subsets, metrics, human-annotation procedures, and appendix generation settings are unchanged. The added critical-reflection row supplies outcomes for an already discussed ablation without documenting a revised experimental design.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds explicit accuracy and rank-correlation results for removing Critical Reflection, supplementing the ablation already discussed in Section 5.2.4. Other ablations and main-text and appendix case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate reporting and five-annotator aggregation. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes multi-agent QG Spearman correlation from 57.47 to 58.47 and its reported gain from 14.67 to 15.60. Table 3 adds the w/o. CR row: accuracy 68.74, Kendall correlation 28.73, and Spearman correlation 38.21. Other reported results, including the appendices, are unchanged; these revisions do not establish a method improvement or experimental rerun.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and Equations 1-5 are mathematically unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about fine-grained alignment evaluation, superior human correlation, ETVABench, and limitations of existing T2V models.

C2.justification: Interpretations of question quality, knowledge augmentation, reasoning contributions, and physics/camera limitations are unchanged. Section 5.2.4's effect-size statements are not reconciled with the revised tables.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, generation settings, annotation instructions, and detailed appendix prompts are unchanged. Both versions retain the same project link and statement that code and datasets will become publicly available.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged, including positioning against existing alignment metrics, question-answering approaches, and T2V benchmarks.

P1.justification: Section 3 corrects small language errors, including 'answewred' to 'answered' and 'parsering' to 'parsing', with minor hyphenation and spacing edits. The section structure and remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains one row, slightly shifting its caption and nearby text, and v2 adds page numbers. Figures and supplementary displays otherwise retain the same content and layout.

improvement.justification: Table 2 now agrees with the 58.47 correlation reported elsewhere and correctly gives a 15.60 difference from vanilla QG. Adding the missing critical-reflection row makes the ablation evidence more complete. These are limited reporting improvements: Section 5.2.4 still claims an 11.2% critical-reflection accuracy gain, whereas the new row implies a 20.53-percentage-point difference, and its QG percentage is also unreconciled.
